items.title: Bessent confirms trade, investment board talks as Trump-Xi summit opens

featured_image.name: Trump will set price floors across industries to combat ...

items.description:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed on Thursday that U.S. and Chinese officials are actively discussing the creation of a "Board of Trade" to oversee bilateral commerce and a separate "Board of Investment" to address Chinese investment in non-sensitive sectors of the American economy, as President Donald Trump began two days of talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing.[1][2][3]

Bessent said the investment board would focus on "nonstrategic, nonsensitive areas where Chinese could invest," according to remarks carried by wire services on May 14. His comments came as Trump arrived in China on Wednesday for the first presidential visit to Beijing since 2017, accompanied by a delegation of roughly 17 CEOs including Elon Musk of Tesla, Jensen Huang of Nvidia, Tim Cook of Apple, and Kelly Ortberg of Boeing.[4][5][2][3]

items.title: UN demands answers after Taliban detains three journalists

featured_image.name: Taliban detains three journalists in Afghanistan, UN says - AL-MONITOR: The  Middle Eastʼs leading independent news source since 2012

items.description:
The United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan on Thursday expressed "serious concern" over the detention of at least three journalists by Taliban authorities on unspecified charges, calling for clarity on the legal basis for the arrests and urging due process protections for the detained reporters.[1][2]

The detentions mark the latest crackdown on press freedom in Afghanistan, where media workers have faced growing restrictions since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. The arrests drew swift condemnation from international press freedom organizations and raised fresh alarm about the safety of journalists operating in the country.

items.title: IPC says nearly 20 million in Sudan face acute hunger

featured_image.name: Almost 20 million people in Sudan still face acute hunger, monitors say |  Reuters

items.description: Nearly 19.5 million people in Sudan — more than 40% of the population — are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, according to a new assessment released Wednesday by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, the global hunger monitoring body. The report lands as the conflict between Sudan's military and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces grinds into its fourth year with no end in sight.

items.title: Trump claims Xi's 'declining nation' remark targeted Biden

featured_image.name: U.S. President Trump Meets With China's President Xi And Attends State Banquet

items.description:
As President Donald Trump wrapped up the first day of his two-day state visit to Beijing on Thursday, he took to Truth Social to reframe Chinese President Xi Jinping's characterization of the United States as a "declining nation" — casting it not as a slight against his administration but as a critique of his predecessor, Joe Biden.

"When President Xi very elegantly referred to the United States as perhaps being a declining nation, he was referring to the tremendous damage we suffered during the four years of Sleepy Joe Biden and the Biden Administration, and on that score, he was 100% correct," Trump wrote. Trump did not specify when or where Xi made the remarks. He went on to tout what he described as an "incredible rise" under his 16 months in office, citing record stock markets, foreign investment, and military strength, while expressing hope that U.S.-China relations would be "stronger and better than ever before".[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Six Arab nations demand Iran withdraw Hormuz claims in UN letter

featured_image.name: Gulf states urge UN action to ensure Strait of Hormuz safety

items.description: Six Arab nations have sent a joint letter to the United Nations categorically rejecting Iran's assertions of new authority over the Strait of Hormuz, escalating diplomatic pressure on Tehran over its ongoing disruption of one of the world's most vital maritime corridors.

items.title: Yemen's warring sides agree to largest prisoner swap since civil war began

featured_image.name: A prisoner swap is a symbolic step towards ending the Saudi-led war in Yemen

items.description:
Yemen's internationally recognized government and the Houthi movement agreed on Thursday to release more than 1,600 conflict-related detainees, the Office of the UN Special Envoy for Yemen announced, marking the largest prisoner exchange since the country's civil war erupted over a decade ago.[1][2]

The deal was reached after 14 weeks of intensive negotiations in Amman, Jordan, and will be carried out with the International Committee of the Red Cross, which serves as co-chair of a supervisory committee established under the 2018 Stockholm Agreement.[3][2]

items.title: Trump and Xi agree Iran must not get nuclear weapons

featured_image.name: Trump-Xi China summit: Trade, Iran, Taiwan in focus

items.description:
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during their bilateral meeting in Beijing on Thursday that Iran "can never acquire a nuclear weapon" and that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open to global commerce, according to U.S. officials — the most concrete outcomes of a two-day summit overshadowed by the more-than-two-month-old war between the United States and Iran.[1][2]

A White House official said Xi expressed opposition to any efforts to charge tolls on vessels navigating the strait and showed interest in purchasing more U.S. oil to reduce China's dependence on the Middle East waterway, Bloomberg reported. China's official readout of the meeting, however, did not include energy among the topics the two presidents discussed, though it noted they talked about the Middle East.[3][4]

items.title: Bolivian miners clash with police in La Paz, demand president's resignation

featured_image.name: Bolivia miners clash with police, explosions rock La Paz as unrest grows |  Reuters

items.description: Explosions rocked Bolivia's administrative capital on Thursday as mining groups marched through La Paz and clashed violently with police while demanding the resignation of President Rodrigo Paz, Reuters reported. Witnesses observed protesters hurling what appeared to be sticks of dynamite as they attempted to force their way into Plaza Murillo, the central square that houses key government buildings.[1][2][3]

items.title: Lebanon demands ceasefire as third round of Israel talks open

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-LEBANON-ISRAEL-IRAN-US-WAR

items.description:
Lebanon opened a third round of direct talks with Israel in Washington on Thursday with a demand that Israel halt military operations, as a U.S.-brokered truce set to expire on Sunday has failed to stop weeks of deadly fighting between Israel and Hezbollah.

The two-day negotiations, facilitated by U.S. officials at the State Department, bring together Lebanese envoy Simon Karam and Israeli envoy Ron Dermer, according to the schedule confirmed by the State Department last week. The talks follow previous rounds held on April 14 and April 23, when President Trump brokered the original ceasefire on April 16 and later extended it by three weeks.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Protests erupt in Havana as Cuba runs out of diesel

featured_image.name: Protests flare across Havana as power cuts deepen amid ...

items.description:
Cuba's energy minister confirmed on Wednesday that the island has completely exhausted its diesel and fuel oil supplies, a stark admission that triggered street protests across Havana as residents endured blackouts lasting more than 20 hours a day.

"We have absolutely no diesel," Vicente de la O Levy said during a special televised address, warning that the country's power grid had entered a "critical state." The minister said the Russian oil donation that arrived in late March — roughly 100,000 tonnes of crude — had been fully consumed by early May, leaving Cuba without any meaningful fuel buffer.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says Xi pledged no arms for Iran, help on Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump says Xi offered help to open Hormuz Strait, vowed not to arm Iran |  Arab News

items.description: President Trump said Thursday that Chinese President Xi Jinping offered Beijing's assistance in reopening the Strait of Hormuz and committed that China would not supply military equipment to Iran, characterizing the pledges as a diplomatic win following a two-day summit in Beijing.

items.title: ICC-wanted senator flees Philippine Senate after gunfire

featured_image.name: PHILIPPINES-ICC-POLITICS

items.description: Philippine Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of crimes against humanity, escaped the Senate building early Thursday after a dramatic standoff that saw gunfire erupt inside the legislative chamber, sending journalists and staff scrambling for cover.

items.title: Iran war could cost US $300 billion, analysis warns

featured_image.name: By the End of the Week, the Trump Administration's War in Iran Will Likely  Have Cost $25 Billion - Center for American Progress

items.description:
The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its eleventh week — is threatening to deliver a $300 billion economic shock, as disruptions to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz continue to drive up energy, food, and transportation costs worldwide, according to a MarketWatch analysis published on Tuesday.[1][2]

The warning comes as new U.S. inflation data showed consumer prices rose 3.8 percent in April compared to a year earlier, the fastest pace since May 2023, fueled largely by surging energy costs tied to the conflict. Average fuel prices in the United States have climbed 55 percent since the war began on February 28, with 80 percent of Americans now saying higher gasoline prices are burdening their household finances, according to an NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll.[3][1]

items.title: About 30 vessels cross Strait of Hormuz with Iran's approval amid standoff

featured_image.name: When will Strait of Hormuz be 'safe' for commercial ...

items.description:
Approximately 30 vessels have transited the Strait of Hormuz with Tehran's authorization since Wednesday, Iran's state television reported on Thursday, marking a notable uptick in maritime traffic through the contested waterway even as negotiations to end the war remain stalled.[1]

An official from the naval branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps told the broadcaster that Iran's stance toward "hostile ships" remains unchanged and that such vessels would not be allowed passage. The IRGC continues to require all vessels to obtain approval before transiting the strait, a practice formalized in recent weeks through Tehran's newly established Persian Gulf Strait Authority.[2][3][1]

items.title: Webb telescope spots most primitive galaxy ever found

featured_image.name: James Webb Space Telescope smashes its own record to find the earliest  galaxies that ever existed

items.description:
An international team of astronomers has used the James Webb Space Telescope to characterize the most chemically primitive star-forming galaxy ever observed — an ultra-faint speck of light from 13 billion years ago whose oxygen content is just 1/240th that of the Sun.

The findings, published in Nature on May 13, detail how the team achieved a definitive characterization of the galaxy known as LAP1-B, located at a redshift of 6.625, placing it roughly 800 million years after the Big Bang during the epoch of reionization. The discovery provides what scientists describe as a direct ancestral link to the mysterious "fossil galaxies" found orbiting the Milky Way today.[1][2]

items.title: US clears 10 Chinese firms for Nvidia H200 chips, but no deliveries made

featured_image.name: Watch NVDA Stock Closely: China Comeback Hits Another ...

items.description:
The U.S. Commerce Department has approved roughly 10 Chinese companies to purchase Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips, but not a single delivery has taken place, Reuters reported on Thursday, leaving a multibillion-dollar technology deal in limbo as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang seeks a breakthrough during President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing.[1][2][3]

The approved buyers include Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and JD.com, with distributors such as Lenovo and Foxconn also cleared to act as intermediaries, according to three people familiar with the matter. Each approved customer can purchase up to 75,000 chips under U.S. licensing terms. Lenovo confirmed to Reuters that it "is one of several companies approved to sell H200 in China as part of Nvidia's export license".[2][4][1]

items.title: Samsung begins cutting chip output ahead of historic strike

featured_image.name: Samsung holds desperate final talks with union over 18-day chip factory  strike that could cost $20 billion — government-mediated summit seeks to  avert industrial action that could hit HBM production | Tom's Hardware

items.description:
Samsung Electronics has begun reducing semiconductor production ahead of a planned 18-day general strike set to begin on May 21, after marathon government-mediated negotiations collapsed without a deal. The company started cutting chip output on Thursday, according to MoneyToday, as more than 50,000 union workers prepare for what would be the first full shutdown of Samsung's chip fabrication lines in 42 years.[1][2]

The move comes one day after South Korea's Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol warned that a strike "must not happen under any circumstances," calling it a threat to the country's economic growth, exports, and financial markets. Prime Minister Kim Min-seok convened an emergency meeting of ministers and pledged to "actively support labor-management dialogue so that this does not lead to a strike under any circumstances".[3][4][1]

items.title: Streeting resigns as health secretary, launches bid to unseat Starmer

featured_image.name: Wes Streeting 'preparing to resign' as Keir Starmer dealt leadership blow  moments before King's Speech

items.description:
Wes Streeting resigned as Britain's Health Secretary on Thursday, throwing down a direct challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership of the Labour Party and plunging the governing party deeper into crisis following its disastrous local election results last week.

The BBC confirmed Streeting's resignation on Thursday morning, capping days of speculation after allies had spent Wednesday night phoning Labour MPs to drum up support for a formal leadership contest. The move came just a day after Streeting held a tense, 16-minute meeting with Starmer at Downing Street, following which the Prime Minister insisted he had "full confidence" in his Health Secretary.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran demands BRICS condemn US-Israel war at Delhi summit

featured_image.name: Tehran calls on BRICS members to condemn US-Israeli aggression on Iran:  Iranian FM

items.description: Foreign ministers from BRICS nations opened a two-day meeting in New Delhi on Thursday, with the war in Iran launched by the United States and Israel on February 28 dominating the agenda and laying bare fractures within the expanded bloc. The gathering at Bharat Mandapam, chaired by Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, brings together diplomats from the group's 11 member states — including Iran, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia, countries on opposing sides of the Middle East conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Xi warns Trump of conflict risk if Taiwan is mishandled

featured_image.name: U.S. President Trump Meets With China's President Xi And Attends State Banquet

items.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered a pointed warning to President Donald Trump on Thursday during their summit in Beijing, saying the two countries risk "clashes and even conflicts" if the Taiwan issue is mishandled, according to a readout published by the official Xinhua news agency.[1]

Xi told Trump that if Taiwan is handled well, US-China relations "will enjoy overall stability," but that failure to do so would put "the entire relationship in great jeopardy," calling Taiwan the "most important issue in China-US relations," according to state broadcaster CCTV.[2][1]

The warning stood in sharp contrast to Trump's warm public remarks at the Great Hall of the People, where the US president told Xi, "You're a great leader. Sometimes people don't like me saying it, but I say it anyway, because it's true." He added, "It's an honor to be with you. It's an honor to be your friend," and predicted the bilateral relationship would be "better than ever before," the Associated Press reported.[1]
